title: AI hardware rebounds from the post-election rout while Nvidia slides on a board probe of its CEO
intro: Monday brought back most buyers who fled last week's post-midterm selloff, with optics, equipment, packaging and power names leading as traders positioned for Applied Materials' Nov 12 results. Nvidia was the outlier, falling after its board opened an investigation into Jensen Huang, while the weekend's news centered on the scramble for data-center power and on China holding back H200 imports.
movers_note: Tracked value rose 2.7% from the Nov 6 close to $28.26T at the Nov 9 close (down 1.7% from the Nov 2 close a week earlier); Coherent (+16.8%), Astera Labs (+13.9%), AMD (+13.3%), Bloom Energy (+12.0%) and Applied Materials (+11.3%) gained most, while only Nvidia (-4.3%), Ibiden (-3.5%) and Super Micro (-0.6%) fell, with SK hynix (+0.4%) and SUMCO (+0.4%) the weakest of the rest.

items.headline: Nvidia's board opens a probe into CEO Jensen Huang over an alleged Chinese intelligence effort
items.summary: Nvidia's board started an independent investigation after reports that Huang was targeted by a Chinese intelligence effort involving Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive; Megaspeed bought over $4.8B of Nvidia chips in two years. Analysts expect the episode to add pressure for tighter China chip curbs, and the shares fell nearly 5% at midday.

items.headline: Chip-equipment stocks lead the rebound ahead of Applied Materials' Nov 12 results
items.summary: Applied Materials jumped about 11% and Lam Research and KLA about 9% as traders positioned for Applied's report, which it has guided to $10.25B in revenue plus or minus $500M. Lam expects 2026 wafer-fab equipment spending in the mid-$150B range and more than $200B in 2027.

items.headline: About 600,000 Nvidia H200 chips sit in Hong Kong as Beijing withholds import approval
items.summary: Beijing has not cleared large-scale H200 imports and is steering Alibaba, ByteDance, Tencent and DeepSeek toward domestic chips, Reuters reported, with total approvals possibly ending under 200,000. A grey-market eight-H200 server was offered at over 6M yuan, about triple a year earlier.

items.headline: Constellation details nuclear deals with Google and Amazon and narrows its 2026 guidance
items.summary: On its third-quarter call Constellation described an 890 MW uprate deal with Google across 11 nuclear units, a 20-year 690 MW power agreement with Amazon at Calvert Cliffs and a 270 MW deal with another data customer. It narrowed 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $12.50-12.80 and agreed to buy the 609 MW RISEC plant for $715M.

items.headline: Anthropic reportedly commits about $3.4B to 1.7 GW of gas generators from OnePWR
items.summary: The Financial Times reported that Anthropic agreed in late September to buy roughly $3.4B of heavy-duty gas generators, plus engineering and construction capacity, from San Antonio supplier OnePWR to secure data-center power. Reuters could not verify the report.

items.headline: Gas turbine orders outrun factory capacity as data centers hunt for secondhand units
items.summary: Global turbine orders reportedly exceed 100 GW against 60-70 GW of annual production capacity, pushing data-center developers toward used units. GE Vernova reported a $197B backlog with gas slots sold into 2032, and Vistra closed its roughly 5.5 GW Cogentrix purchase.

items.headline: TSMC reportedly drafts 3D DRAM plans at Nvidia's request
items.summary: The Information reported that TSMC began planning 3D DRAM under its advanced-packaging organization and is weighing converting an existing plant to memory. TSMC did not explicitly deny it and said it remains focused on contract chipmaking.

items.headline: Micron says Taiwan operations are normal after a report it halted a Taoyuan fab plan
items.summary: Bloomberg reported Micron stopped plans for a $3B-$4.5B Taoyuan plant amid a profit-sharing dispute with a union; Micron did not confirm and said its Taiwan operations continue as normal. Taiwan produces about 60% of Micron's traditional memory output.

items.headline: SK hynix's AI unit buys a $377M Penguin Solutions stake as CXMT revenue soars
items.summary: SK hynix's HYAICO bought convertible preferred shares of Penguin Solutions for $377.16M, about 9.1% on an as-converted basis. Separately, China's CXMT reported third-quarter revenue up 613% year on year on the DRAM shortage.
